key_insight: Foundation model representations from pathology images and transcriptomics are complementary, and multimodal fusion only adds value when neither modality clearly dominates the signal.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI support tools may be more reliable when they combine image and omics data and include uncertainty estimates for out-of-distribution cancer cases.
method: Benchmarked five foundation models on eight classification tasks across two real-world oncology cohorts.
Compared three image-omics fusion strategies against unimodal baselines.
Used conformal prediction to assess trustworthiness and prediction-set coverage.
evidence_signal: The study evaluated whole-slide images and transcriptomic profiles from IH-BC and IH-NSCLC cohorts under distribution shift, finding competitive out-of-distribution performance for FM-based representations.
watch_item: Results come from specific commercial cohorts and task settings, so performance and fusion gains may not transfer unchanged to other hospitals, assays, or cancer types.
paper_title: Probing, Fusion, and Trustworthiness: A Systematic Evaluation of Foundation Model Representations for Multimodal Cancer Analysis
